The material handler was moving a pump casing from a floor pallet onto the maintenance bench. The task was routine scheduled work. Stage of the task: transport or handling material. Method in effect: SW-221 Manual Handling of Rotating Equipment. The task was not being performed as written. The difference from the written method was as follows: the written method requires the overhead hoist for anything above 50 pounds, but the hoist was tagged out for inspection so the casing was lifted by hand. Equipment involved: Pump casing from unit P-118 and the maintenance bench in bay 3. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: normal working order, nothing outstanding. The object handled weighed 75 to 100 lb. Handling difficulty: bulky - hard to get arms around and no hand holds. It was held both hands and gripped underneath. PPE in use: safety glasses, steel toe boots and general purpose gloves. This matched the PPE specified for the task. The event was witnessed by at least one other person. Immediately before the event: squatting at the near side of the pallet with the casing at floor level, feet apart and the second handler squatting opposite. Body position at the moment: squatting. At the moment of the event: the lift was called and both handlers raised the casing to about knee height, the far side was raised faster, the casing tilted toward the near handler, and the near handler twisted to the left to keep hold of it. Immediately after the event: the casing was lowered back onto the pallet, the near handler stayed standing and reported pain across the lower back, and the lift was abandoned. The injury arose from overexertion during manual handling. Load handled: 75 to 100 lb. The load was moved from floor level to knee height. It was held at about arm reach. Assist device: An assist device exists but was out of service. This was a two-person lift. Coordination of the team lift: the lift was called by the far handler, the far side was raised roughly a second early, and the load tipped toward the near handler. Point of contact: lower back on the left side. Force applied from in front. Difference from a normal run of this task: The hoist is normally used for this transfer and had been tagged out since the start of the shift. Conditions at the point of injury: restricted working space. Detail: The bay was congested with parts staged for the rebuild, so the handlers could not stand square to the pallet. The event occurred in the first half of the shift. No overtime was being worked. It happened within the first few minutes. The material handler had performed this task before. A known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. Detail: Risk assessment RA-118 covers manual handling of pump components and identifies loads above 50 pounds as requiring mechanical assistance. No guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Stop-work opportunity: The rebuild could have waited for the hoist inspection to finish, but the unit was needed back in service the same day. At the scene, a cold pack was applied. Detail: Cold pack held on the lower back for about 20 minutes. This was given by a trained first aid responder. Notified: the supervisor and EHS. This happened within a few minutes. Afterwards, the equipment was stopped. Work at the location stopped. The material handler was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
